title: Cover Text Too Close to the Edge: How to Fix It (KDP & IngramSpark) | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix cover text that's too close to the edge
description: Your title or author name sits too close to the trim line and could get cut off. See how much space to leave and how to fix your cover quickly.
platforms: Amazon KDP · IngramSpark · Barnes & Noble Press · Lulu
lead: If your title runs right up to the edge, the printer's blade can clip it. Here's how much room to leave.
error: Text is too close to the trim edge and may be cut off
errorNote: Paraphrased. KDP's cover previewer flags this; IngramSpark mentions it in rejection notes.
why:
Covers are printed bigger and then trimmed. The cut can move a tiny bit, so anything right at the edge is at risk. Amazon KDP asks you to keep text at least 0.125" inside the trim line. SparkPrep recommends 0.25" or more so nothing important ever gets close.

Spine text needs room too: it shouldn't touch the folds between the spine and the covers.
manual: Open your original cover file and turn on the trim and bleed guides.
Find any text, logo or face closer than 0.25" to the trim line (0.125" is the bare minimum at KDP).
Move or shrink it so it sits comfortably inside. On the spine, leave space on both sides of the text.
Re-export as PDF/X-1a:2001 with the bleed included.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.

cta.text: SparkPrep reads the words on your cover, measures how close each one sits to the trim and spine folds, and shows you exactly which ones to move.

faq.q: How far from the edge should text be on a book cover?
faq.a: Amazon KDP's minimum is 0.125" inside the trim line. Leaving 0.25" or more is safer.

faq.q: Can background art go to the edge?
faq.a: Yes. Background art should go past the edge into the bleed. Only text and important details need to stay inside.
